newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Rights groups appeal for halt to Bahrain sentences.
newsitem.headline: Rights groups appeal for halt to Bahrain sentences.

text.p: Two U.S. human rights groups have appealed to the Emir of Bahrain Sheikh Isa bin Salman al-Khalifa to halt the planned execution of three Bahrainis for a deadly arson attack linked to unrest in the Gulf Arab state.
Amnesty International USA and the New York-based Human Rights Watch said in a statement sent to Reuters that they made the appeal in a letter to the emir on Wednesday.
"The crime for which these men were convicted is indeed heinous, but this trial did not meet minimal standards of fairness," the letter said.

It said the government has the responsibility to try the men "before an open criminal court in which they can exercise their rights to counsel and to examine the witnesses against them, and whose judgement they can appeal to a higher court."

A cassation court had ruled it had no jurisdiction over the State Security Court's death sentences against the three Bahrainis, paving the way for their execution. The State Security Court's sentences cannot be appealed.
The security court in July ordered the execution of the three for the March attack on a restaurant in which seven Bangladeshis died.
Bahrain in March executed a man for killing a policeman, in the first such move against an anti-government protestor since political unrest erupted in this Gulf island in December 1994.

The State Security Court has sentenced more than 150 people since Bahrain's government, seeking to accelerate judgements, ordered it in March to try hundreds of detainees held for street protests, sabotage and arson attacks.
Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite community have been waging a violent campaign to demand political and economic reforms. About 27 people have died in waves of violence.
